This file contains only the data preparation, statistical tests, and plotting code needed to reproduce the coefficient plot from the two supplied CSV files.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  comment = NA,
  fig.align = "center"
)
options(width = 78)

document_basename <- "coefficient_plot_reproduction.Rmd"
input_document <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
document_dir <- if (!is.null(input_document)) {
  dirname(input_document)
} else {
  # knitr::current_input() is NULL when chunks are run interactively (RStudio
  # inline execution). Locate the document by name from likely roots so output
  # paths are anchored deterministically instead of following getwd().
  candidates <- unique(c(getwd(), file.path(getwd(), "analysis")))
  matches <- candidates[file.exists(file.path(candidates, document_basename))]
  if (length(matches) == 0L) {
    stop(
      "Could not locate ", document_basename, " to anchor output paths. ",
      "Render with rmarkdown::render() from the repo root, or set the working ",
      "directory to the folder that contains the document."
    )
  }
  normalizePath(matches[[1]])
}
```

```{r load-and-prepare-data, results='hide'}
find_data_file <- function(filename) {
  candidates <- unique(c(
    file.path(document_dir, filename),
    file.path(document_dir, "..", "data", filename),
    file.path(getwd(), filename),
    file.path(getwd(), "data", filename)
  ))
  matches <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]

  if (length(matches) == 0L) {
    stop("Could not find ", filename, ".")
  }

  normalizePath(matches[[1]])
}

table5 <- read.csv(
  find_data_file("Online_Data_Table_5.csv"),
  skip = 49,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
table5 <- table5[
  !grepl("^\\(\\d+\\)$", table5[[1]]) & table5[[1]] != "",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

table8 <- read.csv(
  find_data_file("Online_Data_Table_8.csv"),
  skip = 6,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
table8_cz <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(table8[[1]]))
table8 <- table8[!is.na(table8_cz) & table8_cz > 0, , drop = FALSE]

names(table5) <- gsub("^X\\.", "", names(table5))
names(table8) <- gsub("^X\\.", "", names(table8))

# The renames below address columns by position, so fail loudly if a
# differently-versioned CSV moves them rather than regressing on the wrong data.
if (nrow(table5) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "Online_Data_Table_5.csv has no data rows after filtering metadata; ",
    "check the file and the skip = 49 offset."
  )
}
if (nrow(table8) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "Online_Data_Table_8.csv has no data rows after filtering metadata; ",
    "check the file and the skip = 6 offset."
  )
}
if (!(identical(names(table5)[1], "CZ") &&
      grepl("^Children", names(table5)[4]) &&
      grepl("^RM", names(table5)[6]))) {
  stop(
    "Unexpected column layout in Online_Data_Table_5.csv: expected the ",
    "commuting-zone id, children count, and relative-mobility columns at ",
    "positions 1, 4, and 6. Found: ",
    paste(names(table5)[c(1, 4, 6)], collapse = ", "), "."
  )
}
if (!identical(names(table8)[1], "CZ")) {
  stop(
    "Unexpected column layout in Online_Data_Table_8.csv: expected the ",
    "commuting-zone id at position 1. Found: ", names(table8)[1], "."
  )
}

names(table5)[c(1, 4, 6)] <- c("CZ", "n_children", "RM")
names(table8)[1] <- "CZ"

table5$CZ <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(table5$CZ))
table8$CZ <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(table8$CZ))

table8_match <- match(table5$CZ, table8$CZ)
matched_rows <- !is.na(table8_match)
mobility_columns <- c("CZ", "RM", "n_children")
characteristic_columns <- setdiff(names(table8), "CZ")

mobility_data <- table5[matched_rows, mobility_columns, drop = FALSE]
characteristic_data <- table8[
  table8_match[matched_rows],
  characteristic_columns,
  drop = FALSE
]
analysis_data <- cbind(mobility_data, characteristic_data)

numeric_columns <- c(
  "RM",
  "n_children",
  names(table8)[4:ncol(table8)]
)
analysis_data[numeric_columns] <- lapply(
  analysis_data[numeric_columns],
  function(value) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))
)
analysis_data <- analysis_data[
  analysis_data$n_children >= 250 & !is.na(analysis_data$RM),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
rownames(analysis_data) <- NULL
```

```{r permutation-regression-function}
# Algebraically equivalent re-derivation of perm_test_regression() from
# analysis/mobility_analysis.Rmd: the same DiCiccio and Romano (2017) Theorem 3.2
# HC0 robust Wald statistic, evaluated in batched matrix form rather than a
# per-permutation loop. A future change to one should be mirrored in the other.
permutation_regression_test <- function(
    x,
    y,
    permutations = 10000L,
    seed = NULL,
    batch_size = 250L) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  design <- cbind(1, as.numeric(x))
  y <- as.numeric(y)
  n <- nrow(design)

  if (n != length(y)) {
    stop("x and y must have the same number of observations.")
  }

  # The design matrix is fixed across permutations, so these inverses are
  # computed once rather than inside every permutation.
  xtx_inverse <- solve(crossprod(design))
  sigma_inverse <- n * xtx_inverse

  compute_statistics <- function(response) {
    response <- as.matrix(response)
    beta <- xtx_inverse %*% crossprod(design, response)
    residual <- response - design %*% beta
    transformed_beta <- sigma_inverse %*% beta
    score <- design %*% transformed_beta
    colSums(score^2 * residual^2)
  }

  observed_statistic <- compute_statistics(y)[[1]]
  exceedances <- 0L
  remaining <- as.integer(permutations)

  while (remaining > 0L) {
    current_batch <- min(batch_size, remaining)
    permuted_y <- replicate(
      current_batch,
      sample(y, replace = FALSE)
    )
    exceedances <- exceedances + sum(
      compute_statistics(permuted_y) >= observed_statistic
    )
    remaining <- remaining - current_batch
  }

  (exceedances + 1) / (permutations + 1)
}
```

```{r estimate-models, results='hide'}
estimate_covariate <- function(index) {
  covariate <- names(covariate_labels)[[index]]
  model_data <- analysis_data[c("RM", covariate)]
  model_data <- model_data[complete.cases(model_data), , drop = FALSE]

  y <- as.numeric(scale(model_data$RM))
  x <- as.numeric(scale(model_data[[covariate]]))
  model <- lm(y ~ x)
  coefficient_table <- coef(summary(model))

  set.seed(42 + index)
  perk_result <- perk::perk_test(
    x,
    y,
    B = 1000,
    method = "pearson",
    alternative = "two.sided"
  )

  p_permutation_regression <- permutation_regression_test(
    x = x - mean(x),
    y = y - mean(y),
    permutations = 10000,
    seed = 42 + index
  )

  data.frame(
    covariate = covariate,
    covariate_label = unname(covariate_labels[[covariate]]),
    n = nrow(model_data),
    beta = coefficient_table[2, "Estimate"],
    se = coefficient_table[2, "Std. Error"],
    p_classical = coefficient_table[2, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    p_correlation = cor.test(x, y, method = "pearson")$p.value,
    p_hc0 = lmtest::waldtest(
      model,
      vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC0")
    )$`Pr(>F)`[2],
    p_hc3 = lmtest::waldtest(
      model,
      vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC3")
    )$`Pr(>F)`[2],
    p_perk = perk_result$p.value,
    p_permutation_regression = p_permutation_regression
  )
}

results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_along(covariate_labels), estimate_covariate)
)

p_value_columns <- c(
  "p_classical",
  "p_correlation",
  "p_hc0",
  "p_hc3",
  "p_perk",
  "p_permutation_regression"
)
significant_method_count <- rowSums(results[p_value_columns] < 0.05)
results$significance_agreement <- ifelse(
  significant_method_count == length(p_value_columns),
  "All significant",
  ifelse(
    significant_method_count == 0L,
    "None significant",
    "Disagreement"
  )
)
```

```{r coefficient-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=9, out.width='\\linewidth'}
plot_data <- results[order(results$beta), , drop = FALSE]
plot_data$covariate_label <- factor(
  plot_data$covariate_label,
  levels = plot_data$covariate_label
)

coefficient_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = beta, y = covariate_label)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
    ggplot2::aes(
      xmin = beta - 1.96 * se,
      xmax = beta + 1.96 * se,
      color = significance_agreement
    ),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(color = significance_agreement),
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "All significant" = "#2E8B57",
    "None significant" = "gray60",
    "Disagreement" = "#DC143C"
  )) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title =
      "Predictors of Relative Mobility: Classical vs Permutation Inference",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Replication of Chetty et al. (2014) Table VIII with",
      "robustness check (6 methods)"
    ),
    x = "Standardized Coefficient (95% CI)",
    y = "",
    color = "Significance Agreement"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(color = "gray40")
  )

output_dir <- file.path(
  document_dir, "..", "results", "coefficient_plot_reproduction"
)
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
plot_file <- file.path(output_dir, "coefficient_plot.png")
ggplot2::ggsave(
  plot_file,
  coefficient_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 300,
  # theme_minimal() leaves the plot background blank, so without an explicit
  # fill ggsave writes a transparent PNG on any device that carries an alpha
  # channel (the base png device, i.e. this file's minimal dependency set,
  # which does not require ragg). Pin it white so the portable output matches
  # a ragg-backed render.
  bg = "white"
)

coefficient_plot
```
